commitResults.messageTitle: Merge upstream Gradle support and retire Maven build
commitResults.messageBody: Adopt the course Gradle wrapper and Shadow configuration on master, adapt the entry point and artifact name for Larry, and migrate documentation, editor metadata, and UI tests away from Maven.

Task fields do not require subclass access, and storage test formatting

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find task by searching for a keyword in the task description
Add Checkstyle to detect coding style violations

commitResults.messageBody:
Larry relies on programmer-controlled assumptions in task management,
command parsing, storage, and GUI handling. Violating an assumption can
otherwise cause unclear failures or incorrect saved data.

Add assertions for non-null tasks, valid task indexes, matched command
keywords, supported task types, generated GUI responses, and initialized
GUI state. Enable assertions in Gradle and UI tests to check them during
development.

Add focused tests for TaskList preconditions. Correct inherited import
grouping so the complete verification workflow passes.

The JavaFX merge separates local imports from other imports in Main and
MainWindow. The configured CustomImportOrder rule treats them as one
group, so Gradle verification fails even though behavior is unaffected.

Remove the redundant blank lines so both GUI entry points follow the
project's import-order convention. Limit the change to formatting to
restore Checkstyle without altering runtime behavior.

Task creation parsing combines command dispatch with format-specific
validation for deadlines and events. This mixes abstraction levels in
parseTask and makes changes to one task format harder to review safely.

Move deadline and event parsing into focused helper methods. Keep
parseTask responsible for selecting the task type while preserving all
validation rules and user-visible behavior.

The parser repeats separator text alongside numeric offsets that encode
the same string lengths. A separator edit can therefore leave its offset
stale and cause valid task fields to be sliced incorrectly.

Name the task field separators and calculate each field position from
the relevant separator length. This keeps command syntax and indexing
coupled without changing accepted commands or validation behavior.

Storage record deserialization validates field structure and constructs
task objects in one method. This mixes separate responsibilities and
makes the control flow harder to follow when the file format changes.

Extract record validation and task construction into focused helpers.
Keep deserialize responsible for coordinating those steps and applying
the saved completion status, preserving loading behavior and warnings.

The JavaFX merge separates local imports from other imports in Main and
MainWindow. The configured CustomImportOrder rule treats them as one
group, so Gradle verification fails even though behavior is unaffected.

Remove the redundant blank lines so both GUI entry points follow the
project's import-order convention. Limit the change to formatting to
restore Checkstyle without altering runtime behavior.

Saving tasks uses a manual loop to transform each task into its storage
representation. The loop obscures that this is a direct mapping with no
per-item side effects while preserving order.

Expose a sequential stream from TaskList and map each task through the
serializer before writing. This applies streams to a suitable
transformation while preserving task order and the storage format.
Add assertions for internal invariants
Improve code quality iteratively
Serialize tasks with Java streams

Tasks cannot be corrected without deleting and recreating them.

Add edits that preserve task identity and unchanged details.

Validate task-specific fields and event ordering before saving.

Keep legacy event dates loadable so users can repair them gradually.

commitResults.messageTitle: Improve GUI layout and visual feedback
commitResults.messageBody:
The conversation view gives both participants the same visual weight.
This wastes space and makes Larry's responses harder to scan.

Differentiate user commands from Larry's replies, emphasize errors and
command outcomes, and resize message content with the window. Add the
cat-cafe background while retaining high-contrast message surfaces. Use
a larger circular Larry avatar and more readable text.

EVIL LARRY already has a distinct voice, but edge-case replies and
GUI styling do not reinforce it consistently.

- Extend actionable, in-character responses to invalid input, empty
  results, and storage warnings.
- Add the Unutterable font with its license and credit, plus charcoal
  and crimson styling, responsive messages, and a larger avatar.
- Reject invalid event ordering and keep the farewell visible for five
  seconds before exiting.
- Expand unit and UI regression coverage for the strengthened behavior.

EVIL LARRY's interface and documentation still leave some final polish
and resilience requirements unclear.

- Scale larger conversation text and avatars with resizable windows.
- Ignore accidental surrounding whitespace in user commands.
- Document product naming, launch, and missing-data behavior.
- Credit the reused GUI structure and display font.
- Test whitespace parsing and first-save data-file creation.
